hero.filename: RAF Coltishall Station and Squadron Crests on Hangar.jpg
hero.caption:
Image of the various badges painted on the central aircraft hangar.  These depict the final 'full capacity' status of RAF Coltishall.  From left to right: No. 6 Squadron RAF, RAF Coltishall station badge, No. 16 Squadron RAF, No. 41 Squadron RAF, No1 Group Headquarters RAF, No. 54 Squadron RAF.
I personally took this digital photograph.  I submit it freely for use on Wikipedia, and educational purposes.

images.caption: Housing developer's sign on Hautbois Road Planned as a bomber station, the construction of Royal Air Force Coltishall began in February 1939. images.filename: Entrance to War Graves Plot - geograph.org.uk - 752853.jpg
images.caption: Entrance to War Graves Plot. On the edge of ex-RAF Coltishall (the last surviving operational RAF airbase from WWII, closed in 2006), surrounded by fields still accommodating the now redundant landing aids, ground was set aside by the Scottow Parish Council for burials from the station in 1939. Closed again in 1943 due to a shortage of space, nearly 60 casualties of various nationalities are commemorated on the site > 752880. After the war a Cross of Sacrifice was erected in the eastern section of the plot > 752872. A tiny, brick-built cemetery chapel stands not far distant from the entrance. A red light, to alert aircraft to its existence, is still affixed to its roof.
images.alt: Entrance to War Graves Plot. images.caption:
54 Squadron operated the Jaguar from April 1974 to March 2005 and was based at RAF Coltishall for the whole of this period. While ‘XX109’ in the Norwich museum was a test airframe and did not see squadron service, it seems appropriate that it wears the markings of a very local unit.
City of Norwich Aviation Museum
Horsham St Faith, Norwich, Norfolk, UK

4th March 2020
